report.title: Data Validation Report — P0940 CRDT-Port Project
report.scope_note: Curated report findings linked to the 16 existing dashboard catalogue entries. This is not a transcription of every source assessed in the report.
report.interpretation_note: Findings and limitations paraphrase the report at its issue date. Required checks and project recommendations are dashboard follow-up actions derived from those findings. Report assessment is separate from current API retrieval, model suitability and accepted ontology alignment.

sources.label: DfT port and waterborne freight statistics
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies public ODS downloads under OGL v3.0.
findings: Official port-level freight, cargo, route and arrivals statistics support baselines and comparison.
Most tables are annual; selected port-traffic tables are quarterly.
required_checks: Select the required PORT table and preserve its release and reporting period.
Parse ODS headers, units, port names and classifications before combining tables.
limitations: Annual or quarterly aggregates do not describe live vessel movements.
Granularity and publication history vary between tables.

sources.label: DfT Maritime Statistics Dashboard
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies public visualisation; underlying PORT and SPAS tables are separate downloads.
findings: The dashboard supports geographical exploration and comparison of published statistics.
Underlying PORT0499 and passenger-statistics tables are identified for integration.
required_checks: Retrieve the underlying statistical table rather than extract a chart value.
Keep the original statistical definition and release alongside any comparison.
limitations: The dashboard interface is not a live operational feed.
Direct modelling needs the underlying downloadable data.

sources.label: IMF PortWatch spillover simulation details
sources.access_assessment: Report did not confirm output download from the supplied ArcGIS interface.
findings: Scenario outputs describe potential port, trade and supply-chain impacts for selected disruption durations.
The report identifies potential comparison use for cascading-impact modelling.
required_checks: Confirm access and reuse terms for the underlying ArcGIS resources.
Retain scenario duration, model assumptions and output geography.
limitations: Outputs are modelled scenario estimates, not observed disruption records.
Country-level results are coarser than local infrastructure; automated data access remains to be established.

sources.label: Environment Agency flood-monitoring API
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies public JSON REST access without registration and OGL attribution requirements.
findings: Station readings and warning-area information support environmental monitoring.
Measurements are generally updated at 15-minute intervals; recent historical readings are available separately from latest readings.
required_checks: Preserve station and measure identifiers, units, observation times and reference metadata.
Retrieve historical readings explicitly and retain newly retrieved records when building a history.
limitations: The latest-reading endpoint is not a complete historical archive.
The report describes a beta service without guaranteed service levels or safety-critical assurance.

sources.label: Met Office Weather DataHub
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies API setup and product-dependent access/licensing, including subscription tiers.
findings: Observations and regularly updated forecasts support current-condition and weather-hazard analysis.
Structured products include JSON, GeoJSON and GRIB2; horizons vary by product.
required_checks: Confirm product entitlement, key, usage limits, attribution and redistribution terms.
Keep observed records separate from forecasts and retain issue time and valid time.
limitations: Registration and API configuration are required.
Forecast horizon, update basis and usage entitlement are product dependent.

sources.label: Met Office severe-weather warnings API
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies machine-readable Atom/XML and GeoJSON delivery subject to Met Office licence terms.
findings: Warnings describe hazard type, severity, likelihood, impact, valid period and affected area.
The feed changes when warnings are issued, updated, cancelled or expire.
required_checks: Track warning identity, issue/update times, validity, geography and cancellation state.
Confirm current access and terms; retain permitted snapshots if a project warning history is needed.
limitations: The report found no historical-warning archive for this feed.
A warning concerns potential impacts and does not establish damage at a specific asset.

sources.label: National Highways WebTRIS traffic observations
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies public JSON REST and CSV downloads without registration.
findings: Fine-resolution traffic flow and speed records support road-demand baselines and retrospective analysis.
The report identifies structured site, reporting and data-quality resources.
required_checks: Select and verify the counter, metric, time basis and actual returned dates.
Check missing intervals, sensor outages and release lag before constructing model inputs.
limitations: Records are generally published approximately one month in arrears, so this is not the main live traffic source.
Sensor outages and changing site coverage can leave gaps.

sources.label: National Highways Developer Portal APIs
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies registration, API subscription/key and National Highways feed-licence conditions.
findings: Planned and unplanned closures, restrictions and roadside messages can describe strategic-road conditions.
Reference features and current operational products have different update bases.
required_checks: Confirm the specific product, entitlement, licence and payload schema.
Map event locations to the relevant road links and preserve planned/current status and validity.
limitations: Coverage principally concerns the Strategic Road Network rather than every Liverpool road.
Catalogue availability does not establish that this application has a working subscription.

sources.label: DfT NaPTAN access-node reference data
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies public CSV/XML downloads and API access under OGL v3.0.
findings: Unique access-point identifiers and coordinates support public-transport infrastructure mapping.
Updates depend on submissions and validation by responsible authorities.
required_checks: Preserve NaPTAN identifiers, coordinates and extract date.
Verify relevant node coverage and freshness before associating other records.
limitations: Access-point records do not establish whether a service is operating.
The dataset is not a freight-flow or timetable feed; some nodes may be old.

sources.label: Network Rail Open Data feeds
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies a registered-account route and feed-dependent formats and licence conditions.
findings: Schedules, short-term changes, movements, positioning and reference identifiers support planned-versus-actual rail analysis.
Operational feeds and reference or restriction snapshots have different delivery frequencies.
required_checks: Confirm current registration availability and the permitted feed use.
Associate movement records with schedules and railway reference identifiers before local interpretation.
limitations: The report records registration and public-access capacity constraints.
Not all feeds are real time, and Liverpool freight relevance needs task-specific service/location matching.

sources.label: Local traffic and air-quality sensors
sources.access_assessment: This generic catalogue entry has not been matched to a specific dataset assessed in C1.
required_checks: Identify the actual owner, sensor inventory, access route, history, units and time basis.
Obtain source-specific evidence and permissions before assigning report validation or a connected status.
limitations: The report reviews related national road and air-quality sources, but these do not validate an unspecified local sensor feed.

sources.label: Peel Ports Liverpool marine operational information
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies public HTML/PDF and embedded vessel-board information; no public structured API was identified.
findings: Liverpool-specific notices describe navigational changes, closures, restrictions and marine procedures.
Notices can remain valid, be revised or be superseded over long periods.
required_checks: Confirm permission for automated retrieval and republication before connecting a production feed.
Preserve notice identity, affected location, issue/validity dates and supersession status.
limitations: The report describes research use but restrictions on redistribution and republication without written permission.
HTML/PDF and embedded visualisations need extraction and checking; issue date alone does not determine current validity.

sources.label: Global Maritime Traffic Density Service
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies WMS/raster exports; large bulk downloads require a request and authorised downloads carry attribution terms.
findings: Monthly historical density layers support shipping-corridor, exposure and scenario context.
The report records coverage ending in September 2024 and cessation of AIS updates to this service.
required_checks: Record the chosen layer, month, vessel category and raster/geographic resolution.
Confirm export access and attribution before using a layer.
limitations: Aggregated density cannot identify individual vessels, calls or current positions.
Historical coverage and grid resolution limit current or berth-level interpretation.

sources.label: ONS weekly shipping indicators
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies public XLSX releases and retained superseded versions, with OGL and third-party-rights conditions.
findings: Liverpool-level weekly vessel visits and unique-ship counts support maritime baselines and comparisons.
The series starts in 2019 and is regularly revised or updated.
required_checks: Retain workbook release/version and observation week.
Preserve the difference between unique ships and total visits and verify the Liverpool port mask.
limitations: Weekly aggregates are not live AIS or individual-vessel records.
The data cannot identify berth activity, cargo tonnage or commodity-specific flows.

sources.label: Geofabrik OpenStreetMap network extracts
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies public PBF, Shapefile and GeoPackage extracts subject to OSM attribution and ODbL conditions.
findings: Road, rail, waterway and infrastructure features support a shared spatial reference layer.
Extracts are frequently refreshed, with a dedicated Merseyside extract identified.
required_checks: Retain extract date, OSM identifiers, coordinate reference and relevant tags.
Check local completeness and connectivity before using the extracted network for routing or dependency analysis.
limitations: Contributor updates can lag real-world change; frequent publication is not live operational status.
Coverage and positional accuracy vary by location.

sources.label: UK seaports OpenStreetMap export
sources.access_assessment: Report identifies public HDX geospatial downloads subject to ODbL and OSM attribution.
findings: Thematic port and ferry-terminal features provide maritime spatial context.
The report treats this as a static OSM-derived snapshot that overlaps broader Geofabrik coverage.
required_checks: Retain snapshot date, feature identifiers and source attribution.
Check Liverpool feature coverage and reconcile duplicates with the broader OSM extract.
limitations: There is no operational or vessel-activity information.
A dated snapshot should not be treated as a continuously updated asset register.

recommendations.title: Separate historical baselines from current-condition inputs
recommendations.action: Use each dataset at its actual observation and publication scale. Keep annual, weekly and delayed traffic sources labelled separately from updated observations.

recommendations.title: Confirm access and permission before building an adapter
recommendations.action: Record the product, entitlement, permitted processing, attribution and redistribution conditions. Public viewing is not automatic permission for production republication.

recommendations.title: Retain history rather than rely only on latest endpoints
recommendations.action: Retrieve available historical records explicitly and retain permitted, timestamped snapshots for sources that expose only current readings or changing notices.

recommendations.title: Keep reference networks separate from operational state
recommendations.action: Use spatial identifiers and geometry to associate records, then obtain separate observations or confirmed events for service availability and disruption state.

recommendations.title: Preserve the role of modelled and aggregate evidence
recommendations.action: Label scenario estimates, density layers and aggregate activity as such. Confirm units, geographic scope and task compatibility before comparison.

recommendations.title: Verify source-specific processing before model handover
recommendations.action: WP2 checks access, returned records, time coverage and source quality. Each consuming WP confirms its domain mapping, input construction and scientific acceptance; report ratings do not replace those checks.

provider_notices.summary: National Highways reports a pause in new monthly data provision during infrastructure changes. Historic records within the rolling ten-year window remain available in principle; availability for the selected counters and dates must still be checked.
provider_notices.timing_note: The provider estimates three to four months; a confirmed restart date is not given.
